newsitem.title: USA: Ill House panel advances education funding bill.
newsitem.headline: Ill House panel advances education funding bill.

text.p: An Illinois House committee on Wednesday voted to advance Gov. Jim Edgar's education finance reform and construction bond package, spokesman Thomas Hardy said.
The House revenue committee voted 6-5 to advance the governor's proposal for a 25 percent income tax increase to fund $600 million for schools and $900 million of property tax cuts, Hardy said.
Edgar is "confident" the plan will pass and expects the proposal to be considered by the full house on Thursday, Hardy said.
The plan introduced by Democratic House Speaker Michael Madigan earlier Wednesday calls for raising the income tax rate from 3 percent to 3.75 percent to generate a projected $1.5 billion.
The plan would also take $100 million of new growth in state revenues to finance $2 billion of bonds for a matching school construction program.
House Republicans led by Minority Leader Lee Daniels have consistently opposed the plan, however, contending that school funding could be increased using revenue growth and other taxes.

Madigan had planned to bring the proposal to a vote by last Friday, but opted to delay consideration to this week, leading a spokesman for Daniels to argue that the speaker did not have enough votes to get it through the House.
Republican Senate President James "Pate" Philip has proposed a lesser increase in the income tax and increased teacher accountability.
